S36.01.needs: a question that needs current web sources (web search must be on for the chat)
S36.01.note: The chip is built from the citation link in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx; the chip text is the site name from the source, so no fixed visible label exists for it.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat from the chat screen.
Type a question that needs current facts, such as a recent news topic, and send it.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Look for a small rounded chip with a site name after a sentence in the answer.
Compare with Expected: the claim should carry a marker that names its source.
S36.01.where: Chat screen > ask a question that needs current web sources > read the answer; a small chip with a site name or domain sits right after the claim

S36.02.needs: a question that needs current web sources; a mouse for hover
S36.02.note: Titles come from the source data; a title may be missing for some sources and the chip then falls back to the site name.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover the mouse over a small source chip after a sentence.
Read the bold line at the top of the tooltip that appears.
Alternatively, click the globe button titled Research sources in the top bar, then keep the Sources tab selected.
Compare with Expected: each source should show its title.
S36.02.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > tooltip shows the source title; or Sources > Research sources panel > Sources tab

S36.03.needs: a question that needs current web sources
S36.03.note: For search results the domain shown is the publisher's domain, not the routing host, per packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/citationPublisher.ts.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover a source chip and read the grey line under the title in the tooltip.
Or click the globe button titled Research sources and open the Sources tab.
Read the grey line under each source title in the list.
Compare with Expected: each source should name its publisher or domain.
S36.03.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > tooltip line under the title; or Research sources panel > Sources tab > line under each title

S36.04.needs: a question that needs current web sources; a browser that allows new tabs
S36.04.note: A source chip in an answer is also a link that opens the URL in a new tab (CitationChip.tsx), and a source row with no URL cannot be clicked.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
On the Sources tab, click one source row.
Look for a new browser tab that opens the web address.
Compare with Expected: the source should open at its own URL (the domain is shown under the title).
S36.04.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > click a source row, which opens in a new tab; or click a source chip in an answer

S36.05.needs: a question that needs current web sources, with sources that have a date
S36.05.note: Not all sources carry a date; the tester may see none. The panel shows the raw publishedDate string and the chip tooltip formats it via citationPublisher.ts, so the two formats can differ.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources, then open the Sources tab.
Read the grey line under a source title for a date next to the domain.
Compare with Expected: the publication date should show when the source gives one.
S36.05.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > grey line under a source title; or hover a source chip and read the tooltip

S36.06.needs: a question that needs current web sources
S36.06.note: Retrieved date appears only when the source has a retrieval time; the Retrieved label is also written in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchPanel.tsx.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Click the globe button titled Research sources, then open the Sources tab.
Read the line that starts with Retrieved under a source.
Compare with Expected: each cited source should show when it was retrieved.
S36.06.where: Research sources panel > Sources tab > grey line starting with Retrieved; or hover a source chip and read the tooltip

S36.07.needs: a project with at least one indexed knowledge file; a question the file can answer
S36.07.note: The only icons are FileText for project files (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/ProjectFileCitationChip.tsx), Globe for web sources (CitationChip.tsx) and MessagesSquare for past chats (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/CitationPastChats.tsx). No connector or chat icon was found in the citation chips; icons are not labelled in text.
steps: Open a chat in a project that has knowledge files, and ask a question the files can answer.
Wait for the answer and look at the chip after the claim.
A project-file chip shows a document icon before the file name.
Hover a web source chip and compare: it shows a favicon or a globe icon instead.
Compare with Expected: each source shows an icon for its type.
S36.07.where: Answer that used a project file > look at the icon before the file name in the chip; a web source chip shows a globe icon

S36.08.needs: a question that needs current web sources where the source gives a snippet
S36.08.note: The code shows the source's own snippet, capped at 180 characters (citationPublisher.ts); it is not verified that this snippet is the exact passage behind each claim.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Hover a source chip and read the grey excerpt in the tooltip.
Or click the globe button titled Research sources and read the short excerpt under each source.
Compare with Expected: the excerpt should be the passage that supports the claim.
S36.08.where: Answer with web sources > hover a source chip > grey excerpt text at the bottom of the tooltip; or Research sources panel > Sources tab > two-line grey text under a source

S36.09.needs: a project with a paginated knowledge file (PDF); a question the file can answer
S36.09.note: The page text p. comes from formatProjectFileAnchor in packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts; the preview reads the page from the link in apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx. The chip is an anchor only when a link exists, otherwise it is a non-clickable note.
steps: Open a chat in a project with a knowledge file that has pages, such as a PDF.
Ask a question the file can answer and wait for the answer.
Look for a chip with the file name and text like p. 3 after it.
Click the chip.
Compare with Expected: the file preview should open at that page number.
S36.09.where: Answer that used a project file > click a project-file chip that shows p. and a page number; the project Sources preview opens at that page

S36.14.needs: an account with an earlier saved chat that the answer can recall
S36.14.note: The nav label Previous chats this answer used is an aria label only and is not visible text. The link carries a highlight parameter for the message; whether the page highlights it on arrival was not checked.
steps: Use a chat that has earlier conversations saved, with the past-chat memory feature on.
Ask a question that refers to something from an earlier chat.
Look for the chip with a past chat title and a date after the answer.
Click the chip.
Compare with Expected: the source chat should open and land on the exact message.
S36.14.where: Answer that used earlier chats > look for a row of chips above or below the answer with a past chat title and date > click one to open that chat at its message

S36.16.needs: a question that needs current web sources
S36.16.note: Placement is done by the markdown renderer in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx; it depends on the model's output, so the tester may see chips grouped at the end of a paragraph.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Read the answer one sentence at a time.
Look at where each source chip sits relative to the sentence.
Hover a chip to see which source it names.
Compare with Expected: each chip should sit at the claim it supports.
S36.16.where: Answer with web sources > read a sentence > the source chip sits right after the sentence it supports

S36.17.needs: a question that needs current web sources where one claim cites several sources
S36.17.note: The +N text is built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx, so it has no fixed visible words. Multiple sources depend on the model citing more than one per claim.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web sources and wait for the answer.
Look for a chip with a site name followed by a plus count such as +1 or +2.
Hover the chip.
Read the tooltip, which lists one row per source.
Compare with Expected: all sources that back this claim should be listed.
S36.17.where: Answer with web sources > a source chip that shows +N after the site name > hover it to see every source in the tooltip

S36.19.needs: a saved research report whose sources were not captured (rare; may need a seeded report)
S36.19.note: The notice text is in ResearchReportView.tsx and shows only when the report has no citations but its text has numbered references. Reaching such a report by a normal run is unverified.
steps: Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
Click the Report tab.
Open a saved research report.
Scroll to the bottom under the Sources heading.
Compare with Expected: where a link is missing, a notice should say the report refers to numbered sources without links, instead of a dead link.
S36.19.where: Research sources panel > Report tab > open a saved report whose text has numbers like [1] but no captured links; the Sources heading shows the notice

S36.25.needs: a saved research report with sources
S36.25.note: The Markdown export adds a ## Sources list built in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/research-report.ts; the PDF and Word output was not checked against this.
steps: Click the globe button titled Research sources at the top of the chat.
Click the Report tab and open a saved research report.
Click Markdown, PDF or Word in the top bar of the report.
Open the downloaded file.
Compare with Expected: the file should keep the numbered citations and the Sources list at the end.
S36.25.where: Research sources panel > Report tab > open a saved report > click Markdown, PDF or Word in the top bar
